During this project, the team did not analyze crashes separately by crash types or severity levels due to the limited number of crashes used for the two cities. For the LED conversion, the Somerville data was separated into before (2010–2015) and after (2016–2019) as the LED replacement in Somerville took place between late 2015 and early 2016. The Cambridge data was separated into before (2010–2014) and after (2015–2019) as the LED upgrade in Cambridge took place during late 2014 and early 2015. Variables with a p-value > 0.5 were eliminated from models (after comparing AIC, etc., scores) for negative binomial regression. The crash data analysis included a number of scenarios. 4.2.1.1 General Nighttime Crash Analysis The purpose of this scenario was to compare nighttime crash frequencies between the two cities for the entire nighttime period. This scenario involved the following models developed using negative binomial regression with random effects: • Nighttime crash frequency model for the after period (1). • Daytime crash frequency model for the after period (2). • Nighttime crash frequency model for the before period (3). • Daytime crash frequency model for the before period (4). The four models would enable not only day-night crash comparisons, but also crash frequency comparisons between before and after LED conversion. The before LED conversion models would ideally set up a baseline for the research team to understand potential nighttime crash frequency changes after the LED conversion in the two cities based on equal conditions. For all four models, the team used C1 and C2 roadways for Cambridge and HPMS roadways for Somerville. 52 The purpose of this analysis was to compare nighttime crash frequencies between the two cities for the entire nighttime period. The analysis included the following four mixed binomial regression models: • Nighttime (Table 9) and daytime (Table 10) models for the after LED conversion period. Both models included HPMS roadways for Somerville and C1 and C2 roadways for Cambridge. The Cambridge Indicator variable was used to indicate the city, or, in other words, the LED system used (i.e., non-dimming LED system in Somerville versus the adaptive system in Cambridge). The daytime crash model in this scenario was used for comparison purposes as the research team did not have information on a number of variables that potentially affect crash frequencies. • Nighttime (Table 11) and daytime (Table 12) models for the before LED conversion period. These two models were developed using the same method except for the before LED conversion period. These models were developed for comparison purposes as well.
